title: Thor’s Helmet Nebula imaged on the occasion of ESO’s 50th anniversary
caption: Thor's Helmet Nebula, NGC 2359, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 2359 · constellation Canis Major · about 15000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #5 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A helmet-shaped cloud of glowing gas gives this nebula its name. Thor's Helmet, also known as NGC 2359, lies around 15 000 light-years from Earth in the constellation Canis Major (the Great Dog), and it spans more than 30 light-years.

The helmet is really a bubble. A bright, massive star near its center drives a wind, and as that wind rushes outward it sweeps up the surrounding molecular cloud, a cold reservoir of gas and dust, and inflates this cavity. The glowing structure traces where the star's wind is pushing into its surroundings.

The image was taken with the Very Large Telescope to mark ESO's 50th anniversary, on 5 October 2012, with help from Brigitte Bailleul, the winner of ESO's Tweet Your Way to the VLT contest. Viewers could follow the observations online as they happened, in a live broadcast from Chile's Paranal Observatory.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.21 x 7.24 arcminutes) and distance (15000 light years), the frame spans roughly 31 × 32 light-years. Its light set out about 15,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
filters: 550 nm · Optical B (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
660 nm · Optical V (Very Large Telescope FORS2)

understand.eye: A large telescope's exposure gathers far more light than the eye, so the faint glowing bubble would not look like this by eye.
